subject: Packaging options — slimline vs surge (questions about downgrade path)
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@arborhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@arborhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging question — need clarity on downgrade terms

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Leadership liked the latency and cost numbers, but Procurement wants clear language on two things before we can move to a pilot:

1) If we start on the "Surge" plan (reserved throughput + burst credits) and later downshift to a lower-cost plan, what does that stepdown look like? Any prorated credits or penalties?

2) For the "Slimline" (feature-trimmed) plan, can you confirm which features are removed vs. gated? We need that mapped to product features we use (batching, KV cache retention, observability retention).

Quick background: Arbor intends to run a 90-day pilot for triage routing (~500k tokens/day during business hours) and we want a predictable monthly spend if we need to scale down after the pilot.

Can you send a short playbook that lays out upgrade/downgrade steps, example bills, and any credits? Procurement will also want a single-point contact for contract language.

Appreciate it — Maya

Attachments: none

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@arborhealth.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@arborhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question — need clarity on downgrade terms

Hi Maya — thanks for the note and the clear ask.

Summary up front: we can support both paths you described. Below is a concise playbook (actionable steps + examples). I attached a one-page PDF and a spreadsheet showing a sample month-by-month bill for a 90-day pilot that migrates from Surge -> Slimline.

Playbook (high level)
- Option A: Surge (reserved throughput + burst credits)
  - What you get: reserved GPU capacity sized to expected peak, burst credits for spiky demand (30% additional), plus standard observability (30-day trace/token retention).
  - Downshift: 14-day notice for capacity decommissioning. Remaining unused committed throughput is converted to credit at 60% of the remaining committed value (applies if you terminate before commitment ends). For normal stepdown at term renewal, we prorate at billing boundary and apply no penalty.

- Option B: Slimline (cost-optimized, feature-trimmed)
  - What you get: lower unit rates, disabled live-tracing, reduced KV cache retention (default 6-hour window), and limited per-token debugging snapshots. Continuous batching and quantization recommendations still available.
  - Upgrade/downgrade: immediate switch available; feature toggles are gated and audited. If you move from Surge -> Slimline mid-term, throughput is scaled down to the new reservation or meter-based billing; credits described above apply if there is a prior reserved commitment.

Example scenarios attached (see spreadsheet):
- Pilot A: 90-day Surge pilot with 3-month reserved capacity, then evaluate. If you downshift at day 91 and don't renew, remaining reserved value converted to a one-time credit at 60% value.
- Pilot B: Start Slimline (metered) for 90 days, then upgrade to Surge for Q4 — no penalties, only pro-rated charges at the upgrade moment.

Discounting / concessions
- For pilots that convert to a 12-month commitment within 30 days of pilot end, we can offer a 10% onboarding credit + one month of burst credits (non-transferrable).

Next steps
- I can update the proposal to include the exact legal language Procurement needs around stepdowns. Ben (copied) will propose the concession matrix (percentages / thresholds). Priyom can provide the billing examples.

Let me know which scenario you prefer and I’ll send the updated PDF + DocuSign-ready proposal.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-slimline-proposal.pdf (PDF), surge-credit-schedule.xlsx (XLSX)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Maya Singh <maya@arborhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question — need clarity on downgrade terms

Thanks, Evelyn — quick thoughts on the concession structure and a practical stepdown we’ve used with other mid-market health customers: 

1) Stepdown credit logic (practical)
   - If customer commits to >=6 months and downshifts before commitment end, convert unused reserved months to credit at 60% (as Evelyn noted).
   - If customer signs a 12-month after the pilot, convertible credit increases to 80% (helps conversion).

2) Feature bundling safety net
   - For Slimline, provide a "watch window" of 30 days where observability retention can be temporarily re-enabled for incident investigations (metered at usage). This reduces operational risk and eases adoption for customers who worry about blindspots.

3) Discounting proposal
   - Pilot -> 12-month conversion: onboarding credit (10%), first-quarter discount (5%), and one-time professional services credit to cover a migration sprint (up to $6k).

Priyom: can you paste the sample month-by-month bill in the spreadsheet and add a column that shows the effective unit-rate after credits? That will help Procurement see the net-dollar movement.

Maya: if you’re comfortable, we could provision a non-production Surge pool sized for the pilot and begin a 30-day evaluation. That keeps risk low and lets us show real cost for your workload.

—Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
